front_blocks.md: What are the two main parts of the mammalian nervous system?

back_blocks.md: The central nervous system (CNS): the brain and spinal cord.
The peripheral nervous system (PNS): the nerves connecting the CNS to the rest of the body.

back_blocks.md: The pancreas releases insulin.
Insulin makes the liver convert glucose into glycogen for storage, lowering blood glucose.

front_blocks.md: How does the body cool down when it is too hot (Extended)?

back_blocks.md: Sweating: sweat evaporates from the skin, taking heat from the body.
Vasodilation: blood vessels near the skin widen, so more blood flows near the surface and loses heat.
Hairs lie flat.

cards.front_md: How does the body cool down when it is too hot (Extended)?
cards.back_md:
Sweating: sweat evaporates from the skin, taking heat from the body.

Vasodilation: blood vessels near the skin widen, so more blood flows near the surface and loses heat.

Hairs lie flat.

front_blocks.md: How does the body warm up when it is too cold (Extended)?

back_blocks.md: Shivering: muscles contract, releasing heat from respiration.
Vasoconstriction: blood vessels near the skin narrow, so less blood flows near the surface and less heat is lost.
Hairs stand up to trap an insulating layer of air.
